title: 360-Degree Orbit
description: A 360-degree orbit shot circles the subject through a full turn, usually at a constant radius, always facing them. The background becomes a continuous ribbon while the person stays the center of interest.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Time can feel as if it collapsed around one kiss, one threat, or one product. Unlike a pan, the camera reveals different sides of the subject and changes their relation to every wall.

A full orbit calls attention to space itself; a partial arc can be quieter. It is the wrong tool when you only needed a quarter-turn to change a conversation axis, and the wrong tool if the subject is spinning on a turntable while the camera sits still.
Separate live-speed orbiting from bullet time, which also manipulates time.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lay a circular path, pick a center, coordinate focus as distance breathes. Keep height even unless you also boom.
Do not zoom during the orbit unless you want a different technique. Prompt a full 360-degree orbit, constant radius, always facing the subject, background wrapping as a ribbon of light.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a moment should close around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero. Concrete beat: a couple kisses while the room becomes a ribbon.
Do not also zoom, and do not let the subject rotate instead of the camera.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Arc Left and Arc Right are partial orbits, often about 90 degrees, for axis change rather than spectacle. A Lazy Susan turns the object while the camera may stay put.
A pan never relocates the support. Orbit 360 is a full inspection on an azimuth circle.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Matrix circles suspended action in the rooftop bullet-time sequence: orbit plus time manipulation, so keep the distinction. Vertigo circles Scottie and Judy as the remembered setting appears.
Carlito's Way and American Beauty use live-speed orbits as trap or rapture. Grammar of the circle, not a costume to copy.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Full 360-degree orbit around [Subject], camera circling at constant radius, background becoming a continuous ribbon of light, centripetal romantic or predatory energy. For motion: the camera orbits 360 degrees around [Subject], always facing them, background wrapping as a ribbon of light.

Orbit clockwise 120 degrees around a violinist standing still in an empty circular hall. Keep her eyes near the same point in frame, natural live-speed motion, constant camera distance, no zoom. Columns reveal genuine changing perspective. One uninterrupted eight-second take.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a subject rotating on the spot, or a Pan Left from sticks. The tell is a fixed background with a spinning body, or no parallax.
The fix: camera travels a circle, subject mostly still, background wrapping, constant radius.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is 360-Degree Orbit in film?
It is a camera path that circles a subject all the way around, usually facing them at a steady distance, so every side and every background wall appears.
360-Degree Orbit vs Arc Shot
An arc is a partial curve, often a quarter-turn to change axis. A 360 orbit completes the circle and makes space itself the event.
When should I use 360-Degree Orbit?
When a kiss, a threat, or a hero object should own time. Do not use a full spin if a 90-degree arc would do.
How do I prompt 360-Degree Orbit for AI image or video?
Write camera orbits 360 degrees around [Subject], constant radius, always facing them, background wrapping. Ban a turntable subject and ban extra zoom.
